title: Access token not invalidated on logout — reusable against the data API until it expires (~1 hour)
steps: Login as 9000000029; confirm GET /rest/v1/society_memberships returns 200. POST /auth/v1/logout?scope=global (204). Reuse the SAME access token: GET /auth/v1/user -> 403 session_not_found; refresh grant -> 400; BUT GET /rest/v1/society_memberships -> 200 and POST /rest/v1/rpc/resident_dashboard executes (NOT_A_MEMBER), i.e. JWT still accepted by PostgREST.
expected: After logout the session is fully revoked; a captured access token can no longer reach the data API.
actual: GoTrue /user and the refresh token are revoked, but the stateless access JWT (ttl 3600s, carries session_id) stays valid against PostgREST for up to its 1-hour lifetime. A stolen token keeps full data access for up to ~1h post-logout. Compounds SEC-007 (non-HttpOnly 400-day cookie).
environment: local dev; Supabase local 54321; branch feat/saas-onboarding
api_error: after logout: /auth/v1/user 403 session_not_found; /rest/v1 data calls still 200/execute

title: CORS reflects Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to arbitrary origins
steps: curl -I -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' <api>/rest/v1/ and a GET with the same Origin.
expected: Production must not combine a wildcard ACAO with credentials.
actual: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * returned for any origin; no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. Acceptable for a bearer-token API (foreign pages cannot read a victim's authenticated responses) but noted so production never pairs ACAO:* with Allow-Credentials:true. Web app (Next.js) returns no ACAO (no exposure).

title: Bucket MIME validation trusts declared Content-Type, not file bytes (content-sniffing bypass)
steps: Bucket allowed_mime_types enforce the DECLARED Content-Type only (confirmed: application/x-msdownload -> 415). A file of exe bytes uploaded with a declared Content-Type: application/pdf would pass the allowlist. Live member-context confirmation was blocked by the environment's shared-resource write guard; recorded from config + code review. Same class as CORE-007 (corrupt image accepted).
expected: Reject files whose actual content does not match an allowed type (content sniffing / magic-byte check).
actual: Supabase Storage validates only the declared Content-Type header. An attacker-controlled declared MIME of an allowed type bypasses the allowlist regardless of bytes.
api_error: disallowed declared mime -> 415 invalid_mime_type (works); mismatched-but-allowed declared mime -> not blocked

screen: Production build (not verifiable in this pass)
title: Production build must be confirmed to not serve source maps and to emit digest-only errors
steps: Dev server serves .js.map files (sample .js.map -> 200; 249 .map files in .next/static) and verbose RSC error bodies ('env':'Server','b':'development'). QA rules forbid running next build, so a production build could not be checked here.
expected: Production build serves no .map files and returns digest-only errors with no stack traces or SQL to the browser.
actual: Dev behaviour is as expected (source maps + verbose errors). No secret env values leak in the dev client bundle (only the public anon key). Production build re-check outstanding.
